label: yes
controls_available: The selected full interaction surface accepts Arrow keys or WASD for UP, RIGHT, DOWN, and LEFT, and Space for WAIT; key repeat is ignored.
WIND THE CLOCK starts the autonomous outcome phase; SUBMIT EXPEDITION is administrative.
One outcome-affecting keyboard action can be accepted during the first 1150 ms of each 1800 ms beat. Off-beat presses do not move or attack, while sentries still act at beat boundaries.
Difficulty 5 uses a 9x9 board with 9 interior walls, one crawler, one hopper, two lancers, two hit points per sentry, two player hearts, and a 100-beat maximum.
autonomous_processes: Before WIND THE CLOCK, the board is static and input is not accepted.
After the clock starts, the browser continuously advances the visible beat progress and status from performance.now; synchronization runs every 50 ms.

At every 1800 ms beat boundary, each live crawler or active hopper moves one tile toward the player when possible; a hopper alternates rest/open and shield/chase phases; a lancer remains rooted and damages the player when its phase is STRIKE and the player is adjacent. The beat counter increments and the next action slot opens.
At 100 beats the clock is exhausted; terminal success or death stops further autonomous updates.

grouped_control_modes.name: full-mode active beat action
grouped_control_modes.scope: Every outcome-affecting action occurrence during an active gold beat window across seeds, rounds, and attempts.

clause_i.reason: No policy q using only prior actions and their task times can select an optimal delayed full-keyboard action across this grouped mode. At the same action history, generated boards, enemy positions, and enemy phase offsets differ; the sentry configuration that will be reached after the next beat can require an attack, retreat, direction, or WAIT choice that is not recoverable from I_t. The missing information is the visible, changing sentry state, not merely the fixed beat schedule.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded 300 ms window (the configured three chronological frames) exposes the board walls and exit, player position and health, enemy positions and hit points, hopper shield/open state, lancer phase and danger tiles, the beat label, and the gold progress bar. The one-beat transition is deterministic from that visible state, so a policy g using I_t and this recent window can predict the state at t+1800 ms and choose the delayed-optimal keyboard action. A window straddling a beat boundary visibly shows the sentry/phase change; a single current frame is sufficient when the full state is already displayed.

clause_iii.reason: Use the same grouped mode with Delta=1800 ms. For example, take t=1900 ms after winding the clock: the action is 100 ms into an active gold window, W_t^300 spans 1600--1900 ms and visibly straddles the 1800 ms sentry boundary, and delivery at t+Delta=3700 ms is again 100 ms into an active window. Some such histories remain solvable after no input for one beat (the generator requires a route and a read-only seed-0 replay retained a 19-action route after one no-input beat). During the delay the same visible sentry process moves chasers, changes hopper/lancer phases, and can strike an adjacent player. A direction that attacks or evades a visible sentry at H_t can therefore miss that target or be followed with reduced health at H_t^tau, making its Q strictly lower (or reducing its advantage over no-op) while success remains possible. The loss is caused by non-clock task-state evolution, not by merely having less deadline.

common_visible_process: Beat-boundary sentry evolution is the common witness: the crawler and hopper positions, hopper shield/rest phase, lancer strike phase and danger tiles, health, and the beat progress are rendered in the task UI. That same recent visible state prevents an observation-free action policy, permits a bounded-window prediction of the delayed state, and causes an available attack/defensive action to degrade when the sentries move or strike during the delay.

pre_run.reason: No generated instance admits a successful pre-run solution. Before the clock starts, actions are ignored. After it starts, a run with no outcome-affecting actions can only execute autonomous sentry steps: those steps move or strike sentries, but never decrement enemy health, move the player, or set won. The only code that attacks/moves the player and can set success is act(), so clearing every sentry and entering the stair is impossible without post-start actions. The pre-run rate is therefore structurally 0, below the 0.5 override threshold.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 5 is the 9x9, 9-wall, crawler/hopper/two-lancer, two-health profile; full interaction is implemented with arrows/WASD/Space; the task has a 1800 ms beat, 1150 ms open window, 300 ms observation window, and three frames.

The generator applies the supplied difficulty parameters, randomizes connected walls, positions, and enemy phase offsets across seeds, sets beat_ms=1800/open_ms=1150/max_beats=100, and requires a reachable route.
The browser initializes the visible player/enemy state; active direction actions move or attack, hopper shields can block attacks, and success requires all sentries defeated plus the exit.
Autonomous step processing moves chasers, applies lancer contact damage on strike phases, increments beats, and is driven by elapsed task time at beat boundaries.
The visible UI renders beat status/progress, enemy phase text and health, player/enemy positions, lancer danger tiles, and the current elapsed/beat state.
Input is accepted only in the gold portion of each beat; the full mode maps arrows/WASD/Space to the five grouped actions and starts the clock with WIND THE CLOCK.
The pulse, danger-tile, enemy, shield, and board classes used by the browser are visibly styled in the task UI.
The authoritative replay defines the same initial state, phase calculation, action effects, autonomous enemy movement/strikes, beat increment, and action-slot reset.
Grading replays autonomous beats based on submitted task times, enforces the full-mode keyboard source and beat-window outcomes, and requires the final won state with positive health.
The environment verifier loads the exported result and applies the independent clockbeat replay grader rather than trusting the client state.
The wiring solver waits for each beat and sends one planned key in the active window, corroborating that the intended interaction requires repeated timed actions while the clock runs.
